category_title: Underprepared writers who utilize non-standard technology like cell phones for long-form academic papers
minimal_context: The student is working on revising a 15-page research paper draft in a summer bridge program classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take out your 15-page research paper draft and begin the revision process.

STUDENT: I guess I always thought revision was about fixing spelling.

TUTOR: Look closer at the content. What else do you think needs to be changed?

STUDENT: Revising is way harder than I ever thought. It's like I don't even know what to call what I was doing all through high school. I never knew how bad first drafts really are.

TUTOR: Keep working on it. Try to rewrite the sections that need improvement.

STUDENT: This is just headwork. Homework was easy. You just had to do it. But revising is like giving yourself the worst headache you've ever had in your life. It's like squeezing out your brain cells on paper.

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the revision of the 15-page research paper draft.
options.B: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during instruction on the revision process.
options.C: Use a visual schedule that identifies the revision activities and the reinforcers the student can receive.
options.D: Promote an environment that exposes students to the public humiliation of trial-and-error during the revision process.
